title: Flow Candidates
description: Output of the flow-analyst agent: a ranked, evidenced list of names that unusual options activity says are worth attention today. This is a CANDIDATE list, not a watchlist — the desk still has to reconcile it against the macro brief and the risk envelope before anything becomes tradeable.

scan_config.description: Exactly what was scanned, so a candidate list can be reproduced or compared across days. If the filters move, the list is not comparable to yesterday's and the desk needs to know that.

universe_size.description: How many distinct tickers came back before ranking. Context for how selective the shortlist actually is.

score_rationale.description: Why this ranks where it does, in plain terms. No numeric composite score — an unvalidated score implies a precision this has not earned. Ordinal ranking with a stated reason is honest; a 0-100 score is not.

signals.description: The concrete observations. Each must be traceable to a captured raw response.

source_capture.description: Path under state/raw/ containing the response this came from.

liquidity.description: Non-negotiable gate. A perfect thesis in a chain you cannot get filled in is not a trade. Wide-spread names get rejected here, not discovered at the point of entry.

counter_evidence.description: REQUIRED THINKING even when the value is null: what argues against this name. A candidate with no counter-evidence considered has not been analysed, only found.

rejected.description: Names that scanned well but were dropped, with the reason. This is not bookkeeping — it is how you find out the filters are wrong. A name rejected for liquidity five days running that then runs 20% is a filter problem worth seeing.

gaps.description: Endpoints that failed or returned nothing, and what that means the analysis could not see. Required; an empty array is a claim that the scan was complete.
